title: check and start warn when a code item's mapped doc sits only in an unrelated item's touches
goal: backlog.py check and start warn when a doc that kb/_self/map.csv maps to an item's code is held only by the touches of an unrelated item (not the item's own scope, a descendant, or a dependency), naming the doc and the holder, without warning for shared docs that many items hold (backlog.md, tools.md, maintaining.md, AGENTS.md); a planted pair in test_backlog.py shows the warning, and the real backlog gains far fewer new warnings than the naive version's 872
notes: Left from ST-w676qit6 "backlog.py start names the committed items whose code docs sit outside their touches" (merged from the dropped ST-ei6xrp7n): its worker built this clause and removed it after measuring 872 new warnings on the real backlog, because shared docs such as kb/_self/backlog.md are held by many items. Premise, run before a sprint commits this story: add a code item whose mapped doc is held only by an unrelated item's touches to a temp backlog and run python3 _tools/backlog.py check: it prints no warning today (docs_warnings counts every open item as a holder). Open design: how to exclude shared docs (a holder-count cap or a named list). The backlog.py split sprint SP-tpulmoxh moves cmd_start, cmd_check and docs_warnings into bl_plan: rebase this story's touches onto that module before claiming it.
